title: EBRSO: 6 suspects arrested, accused selling drugs in Baton Rouge - NewsBreak
text:
By Keymonte Avery ,
3 hours ago
BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) — The East Baton Rouge Sheriff’s Office arrested six men accused of selling drugs in Baton Rouge.
According to the sheriff’s office, between March and April, agents conducted surveillance on a group of people who were allegedly selling drugs from multiple locations. During the investigation, agents conducted a controlled purchase of fentanyl from a man, later identified as Chase Chevalier, 31, and a separate purchase of meth from Derrick Ross, 25.
Search warrants were granted for a home, two apartments, and Ross’ vehicle.
During the search, the following items were found:
28 dosage units of Oxycodone pills 14.8 grams of methamphetamine 4.36 pounds of marijuana 1.01 pounds of fentanyl (4,600 lethal doses) 5 dosage units of Hydrocodone pills 20 tons hydraulic press with fentanyl residue four digital scales, three with fentanyl residue two blenders with fentanyl residue plastic bags with fentanyl residue two vacuum sealers boxes of plastic bags $21,536 US currency three handguns two rifles seven 3D printed handgun lowers two machine gun conversion devices From left: Michael Chisholm, Derrick Ross, Chase Chevalier, and Jamarcus Ross (East Baton Rouge Sheriff’s Office) Chevalier was arrested and booked on charges of:
3 counts of possession with the intent to distribute Schedule II drugs 3 counts of felon in possession of a firearm 2 counts of possession of a firearm with a controlled dangerous substance 2 counts of possession of a machine gun conversion device possession of a Schedule I drug possession of a Schedule II drug distribution of a Schedule II drug (aff. warrant) operation of a clandestine lab possession of drug paraphernalia possession of a firearm with an obliterated serial number obstruction of justice Ross was booked on charges of:
4 counts of possession with the intent to distribute Schedule II drugs 2 counts of felon in possession of a firearm 2 counts of possession of a firearm with a controlled dangerous substance possession with the intent to distribute Schedule I drugs possession of drug paraphernalia operation of a clandestine lab transactions involving proceeds from drug offenses money laundering distribution of a Schedule II drug (aff. warrant) parole violation (fugitive warrant) flight from officers, obstruction and traffic offenses (fugitive warrant) Jamarcus Ross, 28, was booked on the following charges:
possession with the intent to distribute Schedule I drugs possession of drug paraphernalia felon in possession of a firearm possession of a firearm with a controlled dangerous substance Michael Chisholm, 37, was arrested on the following charges:
possession of a Schedule I drug possession of a Schedule II drug possession of a firearm with a controlled dangerous substance Two additional suspects, Dymarco Hills, 30, and Randell Severio, 33, were arrested. Hills had a bench warrant for failure to appear on possession charges and Severio had a fugitive warrant out of Livingston Parish for possession of heroin.
“This operation removed a dangerous drug trafficking organization from our community that was responsible for distributing thousands of potentially lethal doses of fentanyl,” said EBRSO Sheriff Sid Gautreaux. “What makes this case especially concerning is the presence of machine gun conversion devices and 3D-printed firearms. These ‘switches’ can turn a handgun into a fully automatic weapon in a matter of seconds, significantly increasing the danger to both law enforcement and the public.”
